lines.text: Step five: run. Is Run greyed out? The reason sits beside it, for example Pick a scan first.
With conditions in place and no red line under any block, Run is ready.
Press Run. On a phone, it sits in the bar at the bottom.
For a long list, a progress line shows while it runs. Then the results header appears.
While it runs, the button beside the progress line ends the run early; the stocks already read stay shown.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
Read the header: Matched N of M. N is green when above zero, and amber when zero.
The time pill says when it ran. Hover over it, or long-press on a phone, to see where the data came from.
The table lists the matches first. Each row says Matched, Did not match, or Could not be read, with the reason.
Could not be read is never counted as did not match.
Auto-refresh runs the same scan again every minute while the page is open. Export downloads the table as a spreadsheet file.
The stocks that did not match are counted here; one tap lists them.
Save matches as a watchlist keeps them under My watchlists.
Show on chart opens the matched chart in place, with only the scan's own conditions drawn.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
Where does the data come from? With your own broker connected: every timeframe, from your broker, paced inside its limits.
Without a broker: Daily, Weekly and Monthly from ATP's stored end-of-day history. These candles carry the label Last close, with the date.
The page says it at the top: Daily scans run on the last close from the end-of-day files; intraday scans need your broker.
After a run, the time pill shows the source: your broker, or the stored end-of-day history.
There is no shared live data. Live data for you comes only from your own broker.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
